comments:

Issue Details
Currently, the mode argument is used to create missing parents too. I would like to change it to only apply to the leaf directory. This is consistent with `mkdir` which doesn't use the `-m ` argument for parents. It avoids unintentionally creating parent directories with wrong permissions. For example: ```cs // Create app data folder with `700` permission. string appPath = Path.Combine(Environment.GetFolderPath(Environment.SpecialFolder.ApplicationData, Environment.SpecialFolderOption.DoNotVerify), "my-app"); Directory.CreateDirectory(appPath, UnixFileMode.UserRead | UnixFileMode.UserWrite | UnixFileMode.UserExecute); ``` @eerhardt @adamsitnik @dotnet/area-system-io do you agree? If so, I'll make a PR to implement this change.

`tar` has this behavior.
```
       --overwrite
              Overwrite existing files when extracting.

       --overwrite-dir
              Overwrite metadata of existing directories when extracting (default).
```

`--overwrite` control in .NET is through `overwrite`.
.NET doesn't have an arg for `--overwrite-dir` but the behavior matches with the `tar` default.

This is a good question, because we _do_ create missing parents. Let's assume someone creates an archive with two entries:

```
1) Directory:    parent/child/
2) RegularFile:  parent/child/file.txt
```

Notice that there is no entry for `parent/`.

When we iterate through the entries, the first entry will be created with `Directory.CreateDirectory` and will automatically create the parent, which did not have an entry. This happens in `TarHelpers.Unix.cs`, line 94 in this PR.
